overview: From 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-11, ethereum-optimism/optimism had 23 new PRs (30 merged), 11 new issues, and 37 active contributors.

topIssues.title: kona-client: the library cannot be built for a no_std target
topIssues.author: yoshidan
topIssues.body:
`kona-client`'s library side — `fpvm_evm`, `interop`, `single` — never references `kona_std_fpvm`; only the two binary sources, `src/kona.rs` and `src/kona_interop.rs`, do. But `kona-std-fpvm` and `kona-std-fpvm-proc` are declared unconditionally in `[dependencies]`, so cargo builds them for the library too. `kona-std-fpvm` reads the preimage oracle over file descriptors (`std::fs::File`, `std::os::fd`) and carries no `#![no_std]`, so a consumer that wants only the library cannot build for a `no_std` target:

```
error: `std` is required by `kona_std_fpvm` because it does not declare `#![no_std]`
```

No feature avoids it today: `client-tracing`, the only one, enables `kona-std-fpvm/tracing`.

We hit this building an Intel SGX enclave. The OP Stack light client in [datachainlab/optimism-elc](https://github.com/datachainlab/optimism-elc) uses `kona_client::fpvm_evm::FpvmOpEvmFactory`, and the enclave is built for a custom `x86_64-unknown-unknown-sgx` target with `-Z build-std=core,alloc`, where no `std` exists at all.

`kona-client` is also absent from `no_std_packages` in `rust/justfile`, so `just check-no-std` does not cover it.

### Proposal

Move both dependencies behind a new `fpvm` feature, gate the two `[[bin]]` targets on it with `required-features`, and have `client-tracing` enable it. `default` still enables `client-tracing`, so the ordinary build is unchanged; only a consumer that opts out with `default-features = false` sees a difference. Adding `kona-client` to `no_std_packages` would keep it from regressing.

We have this working against `kona-client/v1.9.0` and are glad to open the PR if the approach looks reasonable.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestInteropFaultProofs_InvalidBlock`
topIssues.author: maurelian
topIssues.body:
https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/139419/workflows/feb351e1-7e49-410d-a1ee-27a572f0e50e/jobs/5877424

Job `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`, merge-queue run for ethereum-optimism/optimism#23771 (contracts-only change), 2026-11-10.

```
Error Trace: op-devstack/dsl/eoa.go:392
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/superfaultproofs/superfaultproofs.go:1196
             op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/proofs/serial/interop_fault_proofs_test.go:81
Error:       Received unexpected error:
             operation failed permanently after 5 attempts: not found
Messages:    invalid exec msg receipt not found
```

About 10s before the assertion, chain 902 reorged out the unsafe block (13) that carried the invalid exec message tx:

```
WARN L2 reorg: existing unsafe block does not match derived attributes from L1 component=supernode chain_id=902
  err="transaction 0 does not match ..." unsafe=ce53f5..f22801:13 pending_safe=ac50d9..a4c010:12
```

The mismatch is in the L1 info deposit (different L1 origin), so the tx is dropped and its receipt is never found. Looks like a race between sequencing and L1 derivation rather than a code regression. CircleCI insights also shows a failure in `memory-all-kona-op-reth-fusaka` (1/100 runs on develop).

topIssues.title: op-deployer: harden and ship the forge path; make it the default for live deploys
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Make forge the default for the live target and `bootstrap`, and make forge a dependable runtime dependency.

**Correctness**
- `SetDisputeGameImpl` always runs on the Go host ([`dispute_games.go#L163`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/fe7323950e39ded5510a5b18c3458d9f42b73103/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/dispute_games.go#L163), [`#L246`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/fe7323950e39ded5510a5b18c3458d9f42b73103/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/dispute_games.go#L246)), whose fork is pinned at start and can't see contracts forge deployed earlier in the same apply. Add a `runWithBytes` entrypoint and a forge caller.
- Don't construct the Go host or `opcm.NewScripts` in forge mode.
- Preflight that the bundle has `foundry.toml` and the `runWithBytes` selectors, with a clear error on mismatch.
- Never recompile at runtime: run `--offline`, fail if forge reports a compile, propagate `FOUNDRY_PROFILE`. Prewarm the script graph in every bundle producer (Docker, melange, CI, publish).
- Use a per-invocation `FOUNDRY_BROADCAST` directory so concurrent runs don't collide (#18760).

**Distribution**
- Docker and apko images already ship a pinned forge; keep them without solc.
- Keep the [auto-download](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/fe7323950e39ded5510a5b18c3458d9f42b73103/op-deployer/pkg/deployer/forge/binary.go) for Linux and macOS. Drop the Windows release targets (Windows auto-download is broken today).
- Respect `--cache-dir` for the forge binary, give a clear error when offline, and autodetect musl instead of requiring `FORGE_ENV=alpine`.
- Document forge as a runtime dependency, including for Go library users (sysgo/devstack consumers).

**Tests, then flip**
- Run the forge package tests in CI (#21200).
- Add an e2e live apply test with additional dispute games and AltDA.
- Flip the default to forge for the live target and `bootstrap`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: op-node: static peer with /dns4 address cannot reconnect after 7 days once the peer's IP changes
topIssues.author: parkjeongryul
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

`op-node` adds `--p2p.static` addresses to the peerstore only once, at startup, with a 7-day TTL (`op-node/p2p/host.go`, `initStaticPeers`). The reconnect loop (`monitorStaticPeers` → `dialStaticPeer`) dials by peer ID only and never re-adds the configured addresses.

After 7 days of uptime the configured `/dns4/...` address expires. The only addresses left are the ones the peer advertised through identify, which inside a Kubernetes pod is the pod IP. If the static peer then restarts and gets a new pod IP, the node keeps dialing the old IP every minute and never reconnects until op-node is restarted.

The peer's Service ClusterIP is advertised only as a side effect of observed-address activation (`ActivationThresh = 4` distinct inbound observers), so you can't count on it. A sequencer that has just restarted and dials its sibling sequencers itself typically has only 3 inbound observers and advertises its pod IP only.

With `--p2p.no-discovery` and several static sequencer peers, each peer drops silently as it is restarted. Nothing is visible until the last one drops. After that the node gets no unsafe payloads and follows L1 derivation only (we observed up to ~93 min of lag).

Nodes using discovery are not affected, because discv5 keeps re-adding addresses from fresh ENRs (24h TTL, refreshed continuously).

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Run op-node A with `--p2p.static=/dns4/<k8s-service>/tcp/9222/p2p/<peer-id>` and `--p2p.no-discovery`, pointing to op-node B behind a Kubernetes Service.
2. Make sure B has fewer than 4 inbound peers, so it advertises only its pod IP.
3. Keep A running for more than 7 days.
4. Restart B's pod so it gets a new pod IP.
5. A logs `error reconnecting to static peer ... dial tcp4 <old-pod-ip>:9222: i/o timeout` every minute and never reconnects.

Results from our cluster:

| A uptime | Addresses in A's peerstore for B | After B restart |
|---|---|---|
| 1 day | DNS + pod IP + ClusterIP | reconnected in 30–55s |
| 17 days | pod IP + ClusterIP | reconnected in 26s (via ClusterIP) |
| 17 days | pod IP only | not reconnected after 19+ min |

**Expected behavior**

A static peer stays dialable through its configured addresses for as long as the process runs. A `/dns4` static address should be re-resolved on every reconnect attempt, regardless of uptime.

**Environment Information:**

- Operating System: Linux (containers on Kubernetes), amd64
- Package Version: op-node v1.19.1 (go-libp2p v0.36.2); the relevant code in `op-node/p2p/host.go` is unchanged on `develop`

**Configurations:**

--p2p.static=/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-1.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>,/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-2.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>,/dns4/<chain>-sequencer-node-3.<ns>.svc/tcp/9222/p2p/<id>
--p2p.no-discovery
--p2p.listen.tcp=9222

Topology: RPC replicas dial 3 sequencers one way. The sequencers do not list the replicas as static peers.

**Logs:**

static peer disconnected, reconnecting  peer=16Uiu2HAmVArk...
error reconnecting to static peer  peer=16Uiu2HAmVArk... err="all dials failed * [/ip4/10.131.53.116/tcp/9222] dial tcp4 10.131.53.116:9222: i/o timeout"

This repeats every minute, always with the old pod IP, until the replica op-node is restarted.

**Additional context**

- Suggested fix: re-add `addr.Addrs` to the peerstore in `dialStaticPeer` before `DialPeer`, so the `/dns4` address gets resolved again on each attempt.
- Workaround: restart the dialing node (this resets the 7-day TTL), or call `opp2p_connectPeer` with the full multiaddr.
- Open question: the stale pod IP was still being dialed 19+ min after the disconnect, longer than the 15 min `RecentlyConnectedAddrTTL`. We haven't found out why.

**Description**

Adds `ComplianceModule` so deposits and withdrawals can wait for policy clearance, then complete on their original terms. The module holds deferred value, and a replaceable policy decides whether it can move.

**Tests**

The module uses its own `ProxyAdmin` outside OPCM to separate custody upgrade authority from policy management. The policy implementation and broader integration coverage follow separately.

topPRs.title: op-deployer!: run live apply and bootstrap on forge by default
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Stack 2/7, merge in order: #23663 → #23664 → #23665 → #23666 → #23667 → #23668 → #23669. The whole change, with green CI, is #23647.

The Go script host needs EVM hooks that only op-geth has, so it blocks the move to upstream go-ethereum (#20266). op-deployer already had an opt-in forge path for live deployments. This PR makes that path dependable and the default for live `apply` and `bootstrap`. Genesis deployments, the L2 genesis, `prepare` and `continue` still run on the Go script host; later PRs of the stack move them.

**Effect on users**

- Live `apply` and `bootstrap` run on forge. `--use-forge=false` still runs them on the Go script host, until #23308 removes the flag. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed: every broadcast sends one transaction at a time.
- As txmgr did, each transaction gets the node's gas estimate just before forge sends it, a tip of at least 1 gwei, and a fee cap of twice the base fee (at least 1 gwei) plus the tip. Unlike txmgr, forge does not bump the fee of, or resubmit, a stuck transaction.
- forge gets the deployer key in a temporary encrypted keystore that only the user can read, never on its command line.
- op-deployer never compiles. It refuses a contracts bundle whose scripts have no `runWithBytes` entrypoint, and it stops forge as soon as forge starts to compile. So a live deployment needs the contracts release of the same op-deployer release: an `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier release is refused (`tag://` locators were already rejected). The default, `embedded`, works, and `--use-forge=false` keeps the Go script host until #23308.
- A contracts bundle is a forge project, so op-deployer does not trust its `foundry.toml`: scripts run without FFI, with file access only to the artifacts, and forge inherits only the environment variables that it needs (`verify-contract` keeps the full environment, for its API key). Each forge script loads every artifact of the project, about 1.3 GB, so forge runs take one of `GOMAXPROCS/2` slots per host.
- forge's output goes to stderr. A failed script reports its revert reason.
- The artifacts-locators page no longer lists `tag://` locators, which op-deployer already rejects. The manual Sepolia test script no longer offers the Go script host as its default engine.
- The forge download detects musl, uses `--cache-dir`, and gives a clear error without network access. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

**Reasons the diff does not show**

- Each broadcast sends one transaction at a time: without `--slow`, forge waited forever when a node dropped one of several transactions that it sent at once.
- forge runs are not `--offline`: offline, forge requires every solc version of the cache installed even when it compiles nothing. A compile watcher enforces "never compile" instead.
- Every forge run uses its own copy of the compile cache and its own broadcast directory, so that concurrent runs (devstack) do not interfere.
- Bundle builds (Docker, melange, `just forge-build`) run one `forge script` to warm the script cache, and fail when a second run would compile: a single script's compile can choose other solc versions than the project build.
- CI jobs that run op-deployer from the checkout now check out the contracts `lib/` submodules: forge reads the sources to check its compile cache.
- sysgo waits for the L1 transaction index before it deploys chains: geth rejects receipt queries until its first indexing pass, and forge gives up after a few quick retries.
- The test `RetryProxy` gives a client error (4xx, not 429) to the client at once: forge calls methods such as `anvil_nodeInfo` that a proxyd endpoint answers with 403, and the retries held each call for about 40 s.
- The `forge` package tests run in CI only after #23643, which removes the package from the CI exclusion list.

**Reviews**

go-code-reviewer on the transitional code of this PR and the next two. Fixed: the BREAKING CHANGE text named `tag://` instead of `https://`/`file://` bundles, and `--use-forge=false` had no test (a live subtest now covers it).

**Known limits, not fixed here**

Live deploys could keep txmgr by simulating on an anvil fork and replaying, as `continue` does (#23306); the #23300 plan chose `forge script --broadcast`. The RPC URL stays on the command line of forge, which has no environment binding for it. A crash during a broadcast can leave the encrypted keystore and its password file in a directory that only the user can read (forge refuses a password pipe). A forge binary in the cache directory is trusted by its version.

Closes #23302.

BREAKING CHANGE: `op-deployer apply` and `op-deployer bootstrap` run on forge by default; `--use-forge=false` runs them on the Go script host until a later release removes it. `--forge-slow-broadcast` is removed. An `https://` or `file://` bundle of an earlier contracts release is refused for live `apply` and `bootstrap`; use `embedded`, or `--use-forge=false` until the Go script host is removed. Go callers replace `ApplyPipelineOpts.UseForge`, `ForgeSlowBroadcast` and `PrivateKey` with `UseScriptHost` (zero value: forge) and `DeployerPrivateKey`; `pipeline.Env`'s `ForgeClient`, `UseForge`, `L1RPCUrl` and `PrivateKey` with `Forge`; and bootstrap's `UseForge` and `ForgeSlowBroadcast` with `UseScriptHost`. `forge.ScriptCaller` returns `(output, error)` without the recompiled flag, and `forge.Client.SlowBroadcast` is removed. The Windows release binaries are no longer built.

topPRs.title: rust!: Update reth to v2.7.0
topPRs.author: aakoshh
topPRs.body:
Closes #23404. This is the first of the version-by-version reth bumps; v2.8.x and v2.9.0 follow.

## What

Updates reth to v2.7.0 through the `op-v2.7.0` fork branch. The pin is a `rev` on the fork stack ethereum-optimism/reth#34 → ethereum-optimism/reth#35 → ethereum-optimism/reth#40 → ethereum-optimism/reth#41 (`0447ceb`) until that stack merges and `op-v2.7.0-0` is tagged. Two of them carry `op-v2.6.0` patches that v2.7.0 lacks: ethereum-optimism/reth#40 the trie seek boundary fix (`paradigmxyz/reth#28264`), and ethereum-optimism/reth#41 the RPC replay through the block executor (ethereum-optimism/reth#37, a backport of `paradigmxyz/reth#28266`) that #23942's `rpc_replay_settlement` tests depend on.

Changes beyond the version sync:

- API adaptations:
  - `StateProviderDatabase` takes an `EvmStateProvider` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27109`).
  - `CancelOnDrop` moved to `reth-tasks` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27466`).
  - `StateProviderFactory` has a `Primitives` type (`paradigmxyz/reth#26923`).
  - `BlockAndReceipts` holds `SharedReceipts` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27427`).
  - The e2e setup functions folded into `E2ETestSetupBuilder` (`paradigmxyz/reth#27432`).
- `reth-optimism-rpc` vendors reth v2.6.0's `MemoryOverlayStateProvider` for the flashblocks pending state (see How).
- op-reth denies the new `--rpc-cache.max-bals-bytes`, like every other block access list option.
- Two mirrored upstream symbols changed: the proofs buffer's copy of the deleted `MemoryOverlayStateProviderRef::hashed_post_state` becomes a frozen `port`, and the proofs-history `get_proof` copy notes why it doesn't follow upstream's new `spawn_blocking_io_with_state`.
- `rust/UPDATING-RETH.md` gains what building the `op-v2.7.0` fork branch needed.

## Why

Keeps op-reth on a supported reth line.

## How

`paradigmxyz/reth#26923` removed `MemoryOverlayStateProvider`, and its replacement, `state_with_block_appended`, can't open the pending state of a speculative flashblock build. With canonical head N-1, a build can run several blocks ahead: N+1 on pending N, and so on. The tip's header names pending N as its parent, which reth's overlay doesn't know, while its bundle holds every write since the anchor N-1. Passing N fails with `BlockHashNotFound`, and passing N-1 panics on the parent `debug_assert` in `OverlayBuilder::with_appended_block`. The vendored provider layers the tip on `history_by_block_hash(anchor)` as before. The commits show it in order: the compiling API change, a red test of the speculative case, then the fix. `op-reth-test-engine` uses `state_with_block_appended` directly, since its blocks link to real parents in the overlay manager it shares with its provider.

**Review request:** the agentic sweep from `docs/ai/reth-update-review.md` (`reth-update-reviewer`, full-range and forward) has not run on this PR. Please run it. Two leads:

1. `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` is now on by default (`paradigmxyz/reth#27447`), sharing recovered senders between transaction ingress and payload execution. Check that recovery through the cache matches the uncached path for deposits (0x7E) and post-exec transactions (0x7D).
2. Upstream's new `LoadState::spawn_blocking_io_with_state` builds pending state through `state_with_block_appended` for a `PendingStateSource::Block`. Check that every `pending` state query still reaches the vendored overlay through `OpEthApi::local_pending_state`.

## Caveats

- Operator-facing CLI changes inherited from reth v2.7.0. No flags are removed:
  - New: `--rpc-cache.max-blocks-bytes` (2 GiB), `--rpc-cache.max-receipts-bytes` (1 GiB), `--rpc-cache.idle-timeout` (1h), and `--engine.backfill-threshold` (32, as before).
  - Lower defaults: `--rpc-cache.max-blocks` 5000 → 1000, `--rpc-cache.max-receipts` 2000 → 500.
  - `--engine.sender-recovery-cache` is on by default. `--engine.sender-recovery-cache=false` turns it off.
  - `--rpc.gascap` (default 50M) now also caps `eth_estimateGas`.
  - `--rpc.max-tracing-requests`, `--rpc.max-blocking-io-requests` and `--rpc.proof-permits` reject `0`.
- RPC: a state query for a block whose changesets are pruned now fails with code `4444` and "pruned history unavailable: requested N, earliest available M" (`paradigmxyz/reth#27367`). It used to be an internal error (`-32603`, "insufficient changesets..."). Nothing in this repo matches either. External clients matching the old text need updating.
- `alloy-trie` stays at 0.9.7 in both lockfiles. The declared range (`0.9.4`, as in reth) admits 0.9.9, which breaks `reth-trie-common` at this reth version (`HashBuilder::all_branch_nodes`), so don't refresh it with a broad `cargo update`.
- The bump changes code that both proof programs run (revm, alloy and kona's executor). The next kona-sp1 build has a new super-aggregation vkey, and the next kona client build has a new Cannon prestate. Releasing either needs the matching `absolutePrestate` in the dispute game args updated on-chain, before or as proposers switch: a proposer whose proofs don't verify against the configured prestate loses its challenged games.
- `eth/memory_overlay.rs` keeps upstream's three `TODO: Currently this does not reuse available in-memory trie nodes.` comments. We don't plan to resolve them:
  - The file is a copy of upstream, kept close so it can be compared with upstream.
  - The gap doesn't apply to its only use: flashblock `ExecutedBlock`s carry no trie updates, so there are no in-memory nodes to reuse.
  - The copy goes away with #23998, or once reth's API can append a chain of blocks.

## Alternatives

- For the flashblocks pending state, several ways to stay on reth's new overlay were considered and dropped:
  - Rewriting the tip's header parent to the anchor breaks the overlay's assumption that parent numbers are consecutive (`parent_num_hash`).
  - Feeding speculative blocks into the engine's overlay manager would mix unvalidated, cumulative-diff blocks into engine state.
  - Folding the whole speculative chain through `OverlayBuilder::with_appended_block` needs both the chain at the RPC (#23998) and reth access we don't have: `state_with_block_appended` takes one block, and `ProviderFactory::overlay_manager` is crate-private.

## Potential follow-ups

- #23998: transactions in earlier speculative flashblock blocks disappear from RPC lookups, and the RPC's pending value isn't reset when speculative state is cleared.
- ethereum-optimism/reth#22 and ethereum-optimism/reth#28, open against `op-v2.6.0`, need carrying onto `op-v2.7.0` if they merge first.
- Companion: ethereum-optimism/optimism-premium#440, in draft, pins this PR's head.

topPRs.title: op-reth: drop the RPC replay override and pin the executor-routing fork
topPRs.author: einar-oplabs
topPRs.body:
Alternative to #23670 for ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#485, paired with ethereum-optimism/reth#33 (the fork backport of paradigmxyz/reth#28266's executor routing, finishing George's ethereum-optimism/reth#24).

With the fork replaying every block transaction through the block executor, op-reth needs no RPC override: this branch is #23670's integration tests and Lagoon fixtures on top of develop, pinned to the reth fork head `bff7be24` that carries the executor routing. The three canonical settlement tests, the refund-dependent affordability case and both raw-block cases pass against that pin with no `Trace` or `Call` implementation in op-reth; the same canonical tests fail on develop against the current `op-v2.6.0-1` tag, which is the regression they pin. All-features clippy on `reth-optimism-rpc` and `reth-optimism-node` is clean.

One #23670 test case changes shape: the fork's `inspect_transaction_in_block` is now index-based and takes no transaction environment, so the "supplied environment" case becomes a direct replay of index 2 that asserts the settled receipt gas. Raw `debug_traceBlock` and `debug_traceBadBlock` stay on the bare EVM in the fork, so the raw-block cases keep asserting pre-refund gas.

The reth pin moves to the merged fork tag before this lands; after it merges, both op-reth-premium workspaces repin to the merge commit. Review agents (`rust-code-reviewer`, `reth-update-reviewer`) run before this leaves draft; findings and dismissals are recorded here.
